text: When the guests were leaving the warm house on Ushers Island, Gabriel Conroy noticed his wife Gretta standing motionless in the shadow of the stairs, listening to a distant voice singing an old Irish air. <break time="0.8s" /> There was grace and mystery in her attitude, as if she were a symbol of something, and Gabriel, watching from the dark hall below, thought that, were he a painter, he would paint her in that pose. <break time="0.8s" /> Later, as they made their way through the slushy streets toward the hotel, moments of their secret life together burst like stars upon his memory, and he longed to be alone with her. <break time="0.8s" /> He felt that they had escaped from their lives and duties, from home and friends, and were running away together with wild and radiant hearts to a new adventure. <break time="0.8s" /> In the hotel room Gabriel told the porter to take away the candle, for the ghostly light from the street lamp lay in a long shaft from one window to the door. <break time="0.8s" /> While Gretta stood before a large mirror, taking off her hat and cloak, Gabriel crossed to the window and looked down into the street, hoping that his emotion might calm a little. <break time="0.8s" /> When at last he turned and called her name, she walked slowly toward him along the shaft of light, and her face looked so serious and weary that the words would not pass his lips. <break time="0.8s" /> No, it was not the moment yet, he told himself, and he waited, longing to be master of her strange mood, for some sign that she was thinking of him.
